cases.problem: Discarded plastic can enter land and water environments.
cases.cause: Product use, disposal and waste-management gaps contribute to releases.
cases.importance: Persistent plastic waste can affect ecosystems.
cases.connection: Prevention and safer material design consider the whole product life cycle.
cases.improvement: Reduce unnecessary plastic use and design products for reuse and practical recovery.

cases.problem: Industrial methylmercury contamination entered the local food chain.
cases.cause: Contaminated factory wastewater reached the surrounding waters.
cases.importance: Eating contaminated seafood caused serious harm to health.
cases.connection: Less hazardous synthesis and pollution prevention seek to avoid hazardous releases.
cases.improvement: Prevent mercury releases and evaluate safer processes; existing contamination still requires management.

cases.period: December 1952; Met Office history accessed 10 Oct 2026
cases.problem: Smoke and fog accumulated during a severe pollution episode.
cases.cause: Coal combustion, including domestic and industrial sources, combined with weather that trapped pollution.
cases.importance: The polluted air harmed people’s health.
cases.connection: Energy efficiency and safer processes can reduce combustion-related burdens.
cases.improvement: Reduce avoidable fuel use and assess cleaner energy sources alongside emission controls.

cases.period: EPA retrospective, 6 Aug 2018; historical disposal and cleanup
cases.problem: Buried chemical waste contaminated groundwater and affected a nearby community.
cases.cause: Hazardous waste disposal created a long-lived contamination problem.
cases.importance: The case shows why disposal risks extend beyond the factory.
cases.connection: Waste prevention is preferable to managing hazardous residues after they form.
cases.improvement: Reduce hazardous waste at source; containment and monitoring remain important for existing sites.

cases.period: WHO account, 29 Aug 2024; historical site example
cases.problem: Unsafe e-waste processing can release harmful substances.
cases.cause: Open burning and poorly controlled recovery expose people and the environment.
cases.importance: Workers and nearby children can be exposed to toxic substances.
cases.connection: Safer product design and controlled material recovery can reduce risks.
cases.improvement: Use formal collection and safer recovery systems; avoid uncontrolled burning.

cases.type: Documented refrigerant policy, not an emissions inventory
cases.problem: Australia limits bulk HFC imports through a gradual phase-down.
cases.cause: HFC refrigerants can contribute to warming when released.
cases.importance: Refrigerant choice, containment and equipment efficiency affect climate impacts.
cases.connection: Design safer chemicals and assess substitutes over their life cycle.
cases.improvement: Evaluate lower-global-warming-potential alternatives with safety, equipment compatibility and energy use.

cases.period: German Environment Agency guidance, accessed 10 October 2026
cases.problem: Discarded electronics contain both recoverable materials and components requiring controlled treatment.
cases.cause: Mixed disposal makes recovery and pollutant separation harder.
cases.importance: Separate collection supports recovery and safe handling.
cases.connection: Design for reuse and recovery while reducing hazardous material use.
cases.improvement: Use suitable collection and treatment systems; prevent waste through longer product life.

cases.period: MPPCB monthly report, April 2024, Annexure VIII and p.36
cases.type: Historical monitoring report · local river coverage
cases.problem: The report records unsatisfactory water quality at monitored Khan River locations.
cases.cause: The report identifies sewage entering the river and describes treatment infrastructure.
cases.importance: Untreated wastewater can harm river quality and downstream use.
cases.connection: Prevent pollution at source and reduce avoidable wastewater.
cases.improvement: Evaluate process-water reuse alongside effective wastewater treatment; chemistry alone cannot replace sanitation infrastructure.

cases.period: MPPCB revised CEPI action plan; schedules include 2023–2025, publication date not stated
cases.type: Documented action plan · not current air-quality measurement
cases.problem: The plan addresses combustion emissions and fugitive dust in the Singrauli industrial region.
cases.cause: Thermal generation, coal handling and ash management are addressed in the plan.
cases.importance: Air emission controls matter for surrounding communities.
cases.connection: Energy efficiency can reduce fuel demand; pollution controls are also needed.
cases.improvement: Consider efficient energy use and appropriate dust and combustion-emission controls. The plan does not prove that every action is complete.

cases.period: CSE laboratory study, December 2009; sampled sites only
cases.type: Historical site investigation · not a citywide or current rating
cases.problem: The study detected pesticides, chlorinated benzenes and metals in sampled soil and waste at the former factory site.
cases.cause: Legacy pesticide production and waste storage left contaminated materials.
cases.importance: Persistent residues require site-specific assessment and management.
cases.connection: Prevent hazardous waste and choose less hazardous synthesis where feasible.
cases.improvement: Prevent new hazardous residues and assess existing contamination scientifically; no current cleanup status is inferred.
